title: Curve.get_point_position() returns swapped X/Y compared to serialized .tscn data (Godot 4.7.dev1)
body:
### Tested versions

Reproduced in a clean project using the official build (no custom modules, no GDExtensions, no plugins). - Godot Engine v4.7.dev1.official.bf95b6258

### System information

Godot Engine v4.7.dev1.official.bf95b6258 Renderer: Compatibility GPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3070 Ti (Driver 591.74) OS: Windows 10

### Issue description

In a clean Godot 4.7.dev1 project, Curve.get_point_position() appears to return swapped X/Y values compared to the coordinates stored in the .tscn file.

The scene file stores points as:

```
Vector2(0.29969418, 0.06032425)
Vector2(0.60144925, 0.19643795)
```
However, printing the runtime values using:
```
curve.get_point_position(i)
```
produces:
```
(0.060324, 0.299694)
(0.196438, 0.601449)
```
The X and Y components appear inverted relative to the serialized data.

This also affects `curve.sample(t),` which produces unexpectedly high values early in the curve due to the swapped coordinates.

### Steps to reproduce

- Create a new project in Godot 4.7.dev1 (official build).

- Add a Node3D to the scene.

- Attach the following script:

```
extends Node3D

@export var curve: Curve

func _ready():
	print("Raw point positions:")
	for i in curve.get_point_count():
		print(curve.get_point_position(i))
```

- In the Inspector, create a new embedded Curve resource.

- Add the following points manually in the Curve editor:

```
(0, 0)

(~0.3, ~0.06)

(~0.6, ~0.19)

(1, 1)
```
- Save the scene.

- Open the .tscn file and confirm the stored values:

```
Vector2(0.299..., 0.060...)
Vector2(0.601..., `0.196...)
```


- Run the project.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[new-game-project.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/25422647/new-game-project.zip)
